pivots.stem: What did the professor say the sediment cores indicated about rainfall in the settlement's final decades?
settings: That rainfall declined gradually across those decades
That rainfall swung between unusually wet and unusually dry years
That rainfall stayed close to the region's long-term average
That rainfall rose noticeably compared with earlier centuries

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the residue analysis show the large storage jars had mostly held?
settings: Barley grown in the fields around the settlement
Wine brought in from outside the region
Olive oil pressed at the settlement itself
Dried fish carried up from the coast

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the neighboring settlement of Kessara?
settings: It was abandoned around the same time, which points to a cause beyond a single site
It continued to function afterward, which complicates a region-wide explanation
Its tablets refer to Tell Arvani, which helps date the final occupation layer
Its excavation used newer methods that the professor wants applied at Tell Arvani

pivots.stem: What is the professor's assessment of the earthquake explanation for the abandonment of Tell Arvani?
settings: It rests on damage that turned out to reflect gradual decay rather than a single event
The collapsed walls support it, and it is currently the best-supported explanation
The damage pattern fits an earthquake, but one that struck centuries before the abandonment
It may account for some of the damage, but not for the abandonment by itself

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the ground-deformation measurements showed during the unrest episode at the Serrat caldera?
settings: The uplift was centered under the caldera's western rim rather than its middle
The ground rose and then subsided again in a repeating cycle
The uplift went on steadily even after the earthquake swarms had stopped
The deformation covered a much smaller area than the first reports claimed

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the gas measurements suggest about the source of the unrest?
settings: Fresh magma was rising and stalling beneath the caldera
Heated groundwater, rather than new magma, was driving the changes
Gas from an older, cooling intrusion was escaping along reopened faults
The gases carried the signature of magma and groundwater together, pointing to a mixed source

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the caldera's nineteenth-century episode?
settings: Its opening phase resembled the recent unrest, which is why the recent episode drew such attention
It ended without an eruption, showing that unrest at this caldera does not always lead to one
It was misread by observers at the time in a way the professor thinks is being repeated
It left the deposits that let geologists map how far the hazard zone extends

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply about the decision to raise the alert level partway through the episode?
settings: It was driven more by public pressure than by the monitoring data
It was justified at the time, given what the instruments were then showing
It came later than the data warranted, in the professor's reading
It followed a fixed protocol that left the scientists themselves little say

pivots.stem: What did the professor say the pigment analysis revealed about the blue areas of the Verrine Hours?

A cheaper azurite base was covered with a thin layer of lapis lazuli
Azurite appears in the margins, while lapis lazuli was reserved for the central figures
The blue is mostly indigo, blended to imitate the look of lapis lazuli

pivots.stem: What is the main point the professor makes about the workshop that produced the Verrine Hours?
settings: It reused compositions from an older model book for decades
Its choices of material followed each patron's budget more than any artistic rule
Its books have long been confused with the output of a rival workshop in Arden
It kept working in an older style long after painters elsewhere had moved on

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the workshop's surviving account books?
settings: They record what the workshop paid for pigments, giving evidence independent of the analysis
They list the assistants by name, showing how many people worked on a single book
They narrow the book's production to a two-year window
They show the patron stopped paying partway through, which explains the unfinished pages

pivots.stem: What does the professor conclude about attributing the Verrine Hours to Master Anselm himself?
settings: He probably painted the faces, while assistants completed the rest

The attribution holds, on the strength of the page layouts and borders rather than the figures

pivots.stem: What did the seedling survey conducted five years after the cyclone show?

Seedlings were plentiful at first, but few survived their first dry season

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the follow-up experiment indicate about why seed dispersal changed?

pivots.stem: Why does the professor refer to the kanari forests on the mainland?
